title: Loan Portfolio Management
subtitle: Analyse, limit, work out, provide for, stress and report a whole loan book under NBE rules
summary: Move from the single loan to the whole book: portfolio analytics, limits, workout, IFRS 9 staging, stress testing and board reporting, using one Ethiopian bank's 2,000-loan portfolio as a running case.
audience: Portfolio managers, credit risk managers and credit administration managers in Ethiopian banks and microfinance institutions, and loan follow-up officers and branch managers who have completed the Beginner level (or 1.e Level 1) and want to manage the book as a whole.
objectives: Analyse portfolio risk by sector, product, region and borrower group with vintage, migration and concentration tools
Set limits aligned with SBB/87/2024, SBB/88/2024 and a capital-based credit budget under SBB/95/2025
Design restructuring and workout strategies that preserve value and follow SBB/90/2024
Stage the book under IFRS 9 and reconcile it with SBB/90/2024 minimum provisions
Run Ethiopian stress tests and produce portfolio reports for management, ALCO, the board and NBE

runningCase.name: Bank A's 2,000-loan portfolio
runningCase.text: Bank A is a fictional mid-sized Ethiopian commercial bank with Birr 60.0 billion of gross loans in 2,000 accounts, Birr 9.6 billion of total capital, Birr 80 billion of risk-weighted assets and an NPL ratio of 5.8% at June 2026. Portfolio manager Meron Alemu and Chief Risk Officer Dawit Haile must understand the book after the credit growth cap is removed in July 2026. The dataset hides a connected group, Gedeo Trading Group, above the large-exposure limit; an import-dependent borrower, Tana Steel Works PLC, exposed to birr depreciation; a problem loan, Koka Flour Mills PLC, heading for workout; and an IFRS 9 allowance below the SBB/90/2024 minimum. Each module takes the review one step further, ending in a stress test and a remediation plan presented to the board risk committee.

modules.title: Portfolio analytics: vintages, migration and concentration
modules.summary: Read the whole loan book as a portfolio: quality indicators, vintage, migration and roll-rate analysis, concentration and the quality of the data underneath.
objectives: Compute and interpret the NPL ratio, past-due buckets, provision coverage and sector mix of a loan book
Build vintage, migration and roll-rate tables and use them to forecast new NPLs
Measure concentration with the Herfindahl index and the top 20 borrower share
Find connected borrowers and data errors that distort portfolio figures

lessons.title: From the single loan to the whole book
body: A credit officer asks whether one borrower will repay. A portfolio manager asks a different question: what is happening to the whole book, where is risk building up, and is the bank being paid for it? The answers come from a small set of indicators read together, every month, in the same format.

The core indicators are the NPL ratio (non-performing loans as a share of gross loans), the past-due buckets that show what is about to become an NPL, provision coverage (loss allowance as a share of NPLs) and the mix of the book by sector, product, region and borrower size. One figure alone misleads: a falling NPL ratio in a fast-growing book can simply mean that new loans have not had time to go bad.
points: NPL ratio = loans classified substandard, doubtful or loss / gross loans
Past-due buckets: current, 1 to 29, 30 to 89, 90 to 179, 180 to 359 and 360 days or more
Sector, product, region and borrower-group mix, as shares of the book

worked.title: Bank A portfolio indicators, June 2026 (Birr billions)
worked.note: The NPL ratio is moderate, but 4.52 billion sits in special mention, more than the whole NPL stock. That is where next quarter's NPLs will come from.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024, Asset classification and provisioning
regulation.text: Loans are classified pass, special mention (30 to 89 days past due), substandard (90 to 179), doubtful (180 to 359) and loss (360 or more), with minimum provisions of 1%, 3%, 20%, 50% and 100%. Every NPL goes on non-accrual regardless of collateral. Level 1 of this course covers the rules in detail; here we use them as the language of the portfolio.

lessons.tip: Always show the special mention balance next to the NPL ratio; it is the leading indicator the board needs.

lessons.title: Vintage analysis: judging loans by their birth year
body: A vintage is the group of loans disbursed in the same period. Vintage analysis tracks what share of each group has defaulted after 6, 12, 18 and 24 months on the books. Because every vintage is compared at the same age, the effect of book growth disappears and you see whether underwriting got better or worse.

If loans booked in one year default faster than older vintages at the same age, something changed at origination: a product campaign, relaxed collateral haircuts, a new branch network or a sector that looked attractive at the time. Vintage curves are the best evidence a portfolio manager can bring to a credit policy discussion.

example.title: The FY2024 SME campaign
example.text: Meron Alemu, portfolio manager at Bank A, plotted SME vintages from the 2,000-loan dataset. Loans booked in FY2024 had 3.9% of balances 90 days past due at 12 months, against 2.4% for FY2023 at the same age. Digging into the files, she found that a branch growth campaign had accepted merchandise collateral at the top of the manual's range and lent to first-time borrowers with six months of trading history. She took the curves, not opinions, to the credit policy committee.

scenario.title: Reading a young vintage
scenario.situation: Bank A's FY2026 vintage of import loans is only six months old and shows 0.4% of balances 90 days past due, the lowest of any vintage. The business director wants to cite it as proof that the new import product is low risk.
scenario.question: What is the best response?
options: Compare it with older import vintages at six months of age before drawing any conclusion
Agree: 0.4% is the best figure in the book
Ignore vintages and use the overall NPL ratio instead
Wait until the vintage is ten years old
scenario.explain: Young loans rarely default early, so a six-month figure says little on its own. Only a comparison at the same age shows whether the new product is better or worse.

lessons.title: Migration matrices and roll rates
body: A migration matrix shows where balances in each classification at the start of a period ended up at its close. It answers questions the NPL ratio cannot: how much of the pass book slipped into special mention, how much special mention cured and how much fell into NPL.

Roll rates do the same for past-due buckets month by month: the share of balances 1 to 29 days past due that roll into 30 to 59, then into 60 to 89, then past 90. Multiply the current balance in each bucket by its roll rate and you have a forecast of next month's new NPLs. A typical Ethiopian bank manual asks district directors to forecast the loans that will turn NPL over the next two months, every month end, from their watch lists; roll rates give that forecast a number.

scenario.title: Where to send the collectors
scenario.situation: Bank A has four extra follow-up officers for one quarter. The 60 to 89 day bucket holds Birr 0.5 billion with a 50% roll rate; the 1 to 29 day bucket holds Birr 3.0 billion with a 20% roll rate.
scenario.question: Where should the first effort go?
options: The 1 to 29 day bucket, because it is the largest
The 60 to 89 day bucket, because half of it will become NPL next month without action
Pass loans, to keep them pass
scenario.explain: The 60 to 89 day bucket is about to cross into NPL, with non-accrual and higher provisions. Early buckets still matter, but the nearest losses come first.

lessons.title: Concentration: the Herfindahl index and the top 20
body: Concentration risk is the chance that one event hits many loans at once: a sector slump, a regional disruption, the failure of a large group. Two simple measures capture most of it. The share of the top 20 borrowers in the book shows single-name risk. The Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HHI), the sum of the squared percentage shares, shows how spread the book is across sectors, products or regions.

An HHI of 10,000 means everything is in one bucket; a perfectly even spread across ten sectors gives 1,000. Many analysts read values above about 1,500 as moderate and above 2,500 as high concentration. These are rules of thumb, not NBE limits, so track the trend and compare it with the bank's own risk appetite.

visual.caption: Shares in percent: 10,000 means one bucket holds the whole book.

worked.title: Sector HHI for Bank A, June 2026
worked.note: Sector spread is moderate, but one loan in three sits with 20 names. Single-name risk is the bigger issue for Bank A.

example.title: Two banks, the same NPL ratio
example.text: Two fictional banks each report a 5% NPL ratio. Bank A's top 20 borrowers hold 31% of its loans; Bank B's hold 12%. If Bank A's three largest names, together Birr 5.4 billion, all slipped in a foreign currency squeeze, its NPL ratio would jump by 9 points overnight. Bank B would need dozens of small failures to move that far. The NPL ratio looks the same; the risk does not.

lessons.tip: Compute HHI on balances, not on account counts; 500 small personal loans should not outweigh one large group.

lessons.title: Connected borrowers hidden in the data
body: Core banking systems list loans by customer number, so a group of companies with shared owners appears as several unrelated borrowers. Large-exposure rules apply to the group of connected counterparties, so the portfolio manager must rebuild the groups: common shareholders and directors, cross guarantees, shared collateral, intercompany trade and the same contact address.

The cleanest tools are the TIN of each company and its shareholders, the guarantor field and the collateral register. Credit Reference Bureau reports pulled at approval also show the related parties of each applicant.

example.title: Gedeo Trading Group
example.text: In the dataset Bank A's top borrower list showed four separate companies: Gedeo Coffee Export PLC (Birr 0.9 billion), Yirga Agro Processing PLC (0.7 billion), Dilla Transport PLC (0.6 billion) and Sidama Warehouse PLC (0.4 billion). Meron matched shareholder TINs and found that one family owns at least 60% of all four, and that each company guarantees the others. Together they are one group with Birr 2.6 billion of exposure.

scenario.title: Is it one group?
scenario.situation: Selam Tesfaye owns 70% of Hawassa Textiles PLC and 15% of Lake Shore Hotel PLC, which is run by unrelated partners. The two companies trade nothing with each other and give no guarantees to each other.
scenario.question: How should the portfolio manager treat them?
options: As one group, because Selam owns shares in both
Delete the hotel from the dataset
Merge them only if both are NPL
As separate counterparties for now, recording the link and checking control and economic dependence
scenario.explain: Connection rests on control or economic dependence. A 15% passive stake with no guarantees or trade does not by itself make one group, but the link should be recorded and reviewed.

lessons.title: Data quality: the analysis is only as good as the file
body: Portfolio analysis fails quietly when the data is wrong. Common faults in Ethiopian loan files are sector codes chosen for convenience rather than the actual business, collateral values that were never revalued, overdrafts with no expiry date, missing guarantor links and restructured loans that lost their original disbursement date.

Run checks before any analysis: totals agree with the general ledger, every loan has a sector, region, classification, days past due and collateral value, dates are logical, and no customer appears under two numbers. Report the error rate itself; it is a governance finding.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (August 2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual lists the data its credit portfolio unit must hold for every loan: borrower, loan type, date granted, maturity, amount, interest rate, accrued interest, interest in memo, repayments, mode of payment, collateral type and value, economic sector and branch. It also notes that mortgage rights lapse if registration runs beyond ten years, so registrations near that point are tracked and reported yearly.

scenario.title: Ledger does not agree
scenario.situation: Meron's dataset totals Birr 59.4 billion, while the general ledger shows Birr 60.0 billion of gross loans. The board pack is due in two days.
scenario.question: What should she do first?
options: Scale every loan up by 1% so the totals match
Find and explain the Birr 0.6 billion gap before running any ratio
Use the dataset and ignore the ledger
Drop the reconciliation from the board pack
scenario.explain: A gap of 1% can hide a missing branch, written-off loans or off-system facilities. Ratios built on an unreconciled file can mislead the board.

takeaways: Read NPL ratio, special mention, coverage and mix together; no single figure tells the story
Vintage curves compare loans at the same age and expose changes in underwriting
Migration and roll rates turn the watch list into a numeric NPL forecast
HHI and the top 20 share measure concentration; rebuild connected groups before measuring
Reconcile the dataset to the ledger and report data errors as findings

quiz.q: Bank A has gross loans of Birr 60.0 billion and NPLs of Birr 3.48 billion. What is the NPL ratio?
A loan book is 50% trade, 30% manufacturing and 20% agriculture. What is the sector HHI?
Why does vintage analysis compare loans at the same months on books?
options: To remove the effect of book growth and loan age
quiz.explain: Young loans rarely default early, so only same-age comparisons show underwriting quality.

quiz.q: The 60 to 89 day bucket holds Birr 0.5 billion with a 50% roll rate. What new NPL inflow does it imply next month?
quiz.explain: 0.5 x 50% = 0.25 billion.

quiz.q: Which evidence best shows that four borrowers form one connected group?
options: Common controlling shareholders and cross guarantees
They bank at the same branch
They are in the same sector
Their loans mature in the same month
quiz.explain: Control and mutual support make them one risk.

quiz.q: Provision coverage is computed as:
quiz.explain: Coverage compares the allowance with the NPL stock it must absorb.

modules.title: Limits and risk appetite
modules.summary: Turn portfolio analysis into limits: sector, product, single obligor and group limits aligned with NBE large-exposure and related-party rules, and a capital-based credit budget now that the credit growth cap has gone.
objectives: Draft a credit risk appetite statement with measurable limits
Test exposures against SBB/87/2024 large-exposure and SBB/88/2024 related-party limits
Set sector, product and region limits from portfolio data
Use SBB/95/2025 risk weights to build a capital-based credit budget after the removal of the credit growth cap

lessons.title: What a credit risk appetite statement says
body: A risk appetite statement is the board's answer to the question: how much credit risk are we willing to take, and where? It turns strategy into numbers that the portfolio unit can monitor: a target NPL ratio, a minimum capital buffer, limits by sector, product, region and borrower group, and triggers that force a discussion before a limit is breached.

Good statements use a traffic light. Green means within appetite; amber is an early trigger set below the limit, when management must explain and propose action; red is a breach that goes to the board. Regulatory limits are the outer wall, and internal limits sit well inside them.

items.label: NPL ceiling
items.text: Bank A: NPL ratio below 5% by June 2027, amber at 6%

items.label: Capital buffer
items.text: Total capital ratio at least 12.5%, above the 11% minimum

items.label: Sector caps
items.text: No sector above 25% of the book

items.label: Group limit
items.text: Internal 20% of total capital, inside the 25% legal limit

items.label: Related parties
items.text: Internal aggregate 30%, inside the 35% legal limit

items.label: Triggers
items.text: Amber at 90% of any limit

example.title: Bank A's first appetite statement
example.text: Bank A's board had approved a growth target but never a risk appetite. Using Meron's portfolio analysis, the Chief Risk Officer, Dawit Haile, proposed six measurable limits with amber triggers at 90% of each. The board debated the sector cap for domestic trade, then approved 25% with an amber trigger at 22.5%. Domestic trade already stood at 24%, so the first report showed amber, which was exactly the point.

scenario.title: Where to set the internal group limit
scenario.situation: The legal limit for a group of connected counterparties is 25% of total capital. Bank A's largest groups are at 27%, 19% and 16% of capital.
scenario.question: Which internal limit is most sensible?
options: 30%, so no group is in breach
20% with an amber trigger at 18%, plus a plan to bring the 27% group down
scenario.explain: An internal limit inside the legal one leaves room for valuation and exchange-rate moves. The breach must be fixed by a plan, not by raising the limit; an immediate 5% limit would force fire sales.

lessons.title: Large exposures and groups of connected counterparties
body: SBB/87/2024 limits what a bank may lend to one counterparty or group of connected counterparties, measured against total capital. Exposure includes loans, overdraft limits, guarantees and other off-balance sheet commitments, not only drawn balances.

The portfolio unit keeps a live register of every group at 10% of capital or more, tests every new approval against it, reports monthly and escalates any breach at once. Approval memos should state the group total after the new facility, not only the single company's figure.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/87/2024, Large exposures
regulation.text: A large exposure is an exposure of 10% or more of the bank's total capital. Exposure to one counterparty or group of connected counterparties may not exceed 25% of total capital. Federal and regional governments and their enterprises, government-guaranteed portions, NBE and intraday interbank exposures are exempt. Banks report large exposures monthly within 20 days and report breaches immediately.

worked.title: Testing Gedeo Trading Group (Birr billions)
worked.note: Bank A is in breach once the four companies are grouped. It must report the breach and agree a plan: repayments, a participation sold to another bank, or extra capital.

scenario.title: A new request from the group
scenario.situation: Dilla Transport PLC, part of the Gedeo group, asks for a Birr 150 million truck loan with excellent collateral. The relationship manager argues that Dilla alone is only 6% of capital.
scenario.question: What should the committee decide?
options: Approve because the collateral is excellent
Approve and split it across two branches
Decline or defer: the group is already above 25%, and collateral does not cure a group limit breach
scenario.explain: The limit applies to the group. Collateral protects recovery but does not reduce the exposure counted under SBB/87/2024, and splitting the loan only hides it.

lessons.title: Related-party limits
body: Loans to the bank's own shareholders, directors, executives and their businesses carry a special risk: weaker scrutiny. SBB/88/2024 limits these exposures and demands arm's-length terms, so a related party may not get a lower rate, weaker collateral or longer grace than an ordinary customer.

The portfolio unit keeps a related-party list, refreshed when shareholders or directors change, and flags every exposure to it. Restructuring or writing off a related-party loan is a sensitive decision that a typical bank manual also reserves for the board above Birr 15 million.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/88/2024, Related party transactions
regulation.text: Related parties include shareholders with 2% or more, directors, senior executives and their related businesses. Exposure to one related party may not exceed 15% of total capital, and to all related parties together 35%. Terms must be at arm's length, and transactions above Birr 15 million need board approval after an Audit Committee opinion.

worked.title: Bank A related-party headroom (Birr billions)

rows.label: New request from Entoto Logistics PLC

worked.note: Entoto Logistics, 40% owned by a director, is within the single-party limit at 1.2 billion, but the new loan would push the aggregate above 35%.

scenario.title: The director's company asks for a discount
scenario.situation: Entoto Logistics PLC, 40% owned by director Ermias Kebede, asks to reduce its proposed request to Birr 0.2 billion so it fits the aggregate limit, priced 2 points below Bank A's standard rate for its risk grade.
scenario.question: What should the credit committee do?
options: Approve only at the standard rate and terms for the risk grade, with board approval after an Audit Committee opinion
Approve: it now fits the limit
Approve and keep the director's link out of the file
Let the director vote on the request
scenario.explain: Fitting the limit is not enough: terms must be at arm's length, and the amount is above Birr 15 million, so board approval after an Audit Committee opinion is needed. The director must not take part.

lessons.title: Sector, product and region limits
body: Sector limits come from three questions: how large is the sector in the economy and in the bank's deposit base, how risky has it been in the bank's own data, and how correlated is it with other sectors already in the book? Import, manufacturing using imported inputs, and building and construction all suffer together when foreign currency is scarce or the birr falls, so they should be read as one risk cluster.

Product and region limits follow the same logic. A region limit protects against drought or disruption that halts trade in one area; a product limit protects against a new product whose loss history is still short.

visual.caption: Bank A sector exposure against proposed limits (course example)

example.title: Construction above its new limit
example.text: Bank A's proposed limit for building and construction is 12%, but the sector already stands at 14% of the book, Birr 8.4 billion. Meron did not recommend calling loans. She proposed that new construction approvals stop above Birr 50 million per project, that maturing facilities run down, and that the sector reach 12% within 18 months as the rest of the book grows. A limit is a direction of travel as much as a ceiling.

worked.title: How quickly does a run-down reach the limit? (Birr billions)

rows.label: Book growth over 18 months, other sectors

lessons.title: Capital as the credit budget
body: Under SBB/95/2025 every loan consumes capital according to its risk weight. Capital consumed equals the loan times its risk weight times the minimum total capital ratio. This makes capital the true budget for lending: two loans of the same size can use very different amounts of it.

A capital-based budget tells each business line how much risk-weighted assets it may add next year, given the capital the bank expects to have and the buffer the board wants. Pricing should cover the cost of the capital each loan consumes.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/95/2025, Risk-based capital adequacy
regulation.text: Banks must hold Common Equity Tier 1 of at least 7%, Tier 1 of at least 9% and total capital of at least 11% of risk-weighted assets. Under the standardised approach, unrated corporates carry a 100% risk weight, unrated SMEs with sales under Birr 90 million 85%, regulatory retail 75%, qualifying residential mortgages 35%, and defaulted exposures 100% or 150%. The directive took effect on 10 November 2025, with full compliance by 31 December 2026.

visual.caption: Use the bank's internal target (12.5% at Bank A) to include the buffer.

rows.label: Unrated SME, sales under Birr 90 million, 85%
Bank A RWA headroom: capital 10.8 / 12.5% target = 86.4, less 80.0 now

worked.note: A defaulted loan at 150% uses half as much capital again as the same loan to a performing unrated corporate, and over four times a qualifying mortgage. Fixing NPLs releases lending capacity.

lessons.title: Lending after the credit growth cap
body: Until July 2026 NBE's credit growth cap was the binding limit on how fast Ethiopian banks could lend. At MPC meeting No. 7 on 13 July 2026 the NBE Board removed the cap, a temporary transition tool, raised the National Bank Rate to 16% and introduced a targeted reserve requirement that NBE may impose on individual banks based on their loan-to-deposit ratio.

With the cap gone, growth is limited by capital, liquidity, funding cost and the bank's own risk appetite. That puts the internal credit budget at the centre. Banks that grow fast with a high loan-to-deposit ratio risk an extra reserve requirement, so the budget must look at funding as well as capital. Trainers should update these settings from the latest MPC release.

regulation.source: NBE Monetary Policy Committee meeting No. 7 (13 July 2026)
regulation.text: The credit growth cap was removed; the National Bank Rate rose by 1 point to 16% with the corridor of plus or minus 3 points unchanged; a targeted additional reserve requirement may be imposed on individual banks based on their loan-to-deposit ratio. The release reported a private-bank loan-to-deposit ratio of 72.7%.

scenario.title: Branch growth plans after the cap
scenario.situation: Bank A's business units ask for 40% loan growth in FY2027, mostly unrated corporate loans. Capital headroom supports about Birr 6.4 billion of RWA, and Bank A's loan-to-deposit ratio is already 76.9%, above the private-bank figure of 72.7%.
scenario.question: What should the portfolio manager recommend?
options: Allocate growth within the capital headroom and deposit growth, favouring lower risk-weight segments, and watch the loan-to-deposit ratio
Ask NBE to reinstate the cap
scenario.explain: 40% growth, about Birr 24 billion, would need far more capital than the headroom and would push the loan-to-deposit ratio up. The internal budget now does the job the cap used to do.

example.title: A capital budget by business line
example.text: Dawit Haile split Bank A's Birr 6.4 billion RWA headroom: corporate Birr 3.0 billion, SME Birr 2.0 billion (about Birr 2.35 billion of loans at 85%), retail and mortgages Birr 1.0 billion, and a Birr 0.4 billion reserve for drawdowns on approved facilities. Each unit's growth target was then set in loans, not just in a percentage.

takeaways: A risk appetite statement turns strategy into measurable limits with amber triggers
SBB/87/2024 counts the whole group of connected counterparties against 25% of total capital
SBB/88/2024 caps related parties at 15% each and 35% in aggregate, at arm's length
Sector limits should treat correlated sectors, such as import-dependent ones, as one cluster
With the credit cap removed, capital under SBB/95/2025 and funding set the credit budget

quiz.q: Bank A's total capital is Birr 9.6 billion. What is the SBB/87/2024 limit for one group?
quiz.explain: 25% x 9.6 = 2.40 billion.

quiz.q: Which exposure is exempt from the SBB/87/2024 large-exposure limit?
options: A loan to a private PLC with excellent collateral
The government-guaranteed portion of an exposure
A loan to a director's company
An overdraft to a large importer
quiz.explain: Government-guaranteed portions are among the listed exemptions.

quiz.q: A related-party transaction of Birr 40 million under SBB/88/2024 needs:
options: No approval if collateral is adequate
Board approval after an Audit Committee opinion
quiz.explain: Above Birr 15 million the board approves after an Audit Committee opinion.

quiz.q: Capital consumed at 11% by a Birr 200 million loan to an unrated SME with sales under Birr 90 million:
What did MPC meeting No. 7 in July 2026 introduce alongside removing the credit growth cap?
options: A targeted reserve requirement linked to each bank's loan-to-deposit ratio
quiz.explain: NBE may impose an additional reserve requirement based on the loan-to-deposit ratio.

quiz.q: Why should import, import-dependent manufacturing and construction be read as one cluster?
options: They have the same interest rate
They all suffer together when foreign currency is scarce or the birr falls
quiz.explain: Correlated sectors concentrate risk even if each is under its own limit.

modules.title: Workout and restructuring
modules.summary: Design workout strategies that preserve value: viability assessment, restructuring options, NBE treatment of restructured loans, debt-to-asset swaps, foreclosure and write-off.
objectives: Move a problem loan from watch list to workout through the bank's escalation steps
Assess viability and compare the value of rescue with foreclosure
Apply SBB/90/2024 rules on non-accrual, cross-default and restructured loans
Manage debt-to-asset swaps, foreclosed assets and write-off

lessons.title: From watch list to workout
body: Workout is a process, not an event: restoring a problem loan through corrective action that improves the borrower's capacity and prevents loss. It starts long before default, when follow-up officers place a borrower on the watch list and the relationship manager begins structured contact.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual moves a file to the central workout unit when the loan becomes non-performing under SBB/90/2024, when a credit committee identifies an adverse condition before default, or when the portfolio unit picks it from early warning signals. The workout unit reviews regular loans monthly and loans in arrears every two weeks.

items.label: Call and visit
items.text: Within 30 days of the missed payment; ask for settlement within 15 days

items.label: First reminder
items.text: Written; pay within 30 days

items.label: Second reminder
items.text: After two weeks without response; pay within 15 days; meeting

items.label: Last reminder
items.text: Legal action if no payment within 7 days

items.label: Workout file
items.text: Negotiation, then committee decision: restructure, liquidate or legal action

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (August 2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual sets this reminder sequence, asks district directors to forecast the loans that will turn NPL over the next two months every month end from their watch lists, and requires that every oral promise made in negotiation be recorded in writing in the loan file.

Overdraft: 60, no free collateral, at 50% (Bank A policy: same category)

worked.note: Because the NPL is 20% or more of Koka's exposure, the overdraft cannot stay performing. Bank A's policy places it in the same category as the defaulted loan, the conservative reading.

example.title: Koka Flour Mills slips
example.text: Koka Flour Mills PLC in Adama borrowed Birr 240 million for a new milling line and working capital. When wheat prices jumped and a large buyer paid late, it missed three quarterly installments. The relationship manager called and visited within the first month, sent the three reminder letters on schedule and logged each promise. By day 200 the file went to the workout unit with a complete history, which made the negotiation that followed far easier.

lessons.title: Is the business viable?
body: The first workout question is not how to collect but whether the business can live. A viable business has a product people still buy, a margin that covers its operating costs, and a cash flow that can service a reasonable debt once the cause of distress is fixed. A non-viable one consumes more of the bank's money the longer it is kept alive.

The workout analyst rebuilds the cash flow of the main business and other income, visits the site, checks the collateral's registration, insurance and limitation period, and separates the symptoms of distress, such as arrears, from the causes, such as a lost buyer, an input price shock or weak management.

left.title: Viable: restructure
items: Operating cash flow positive before debt service
Cause of distress identified and fixable
Owners cooperative and willing to inject funds

right.title: Not viable: exit
items: Operating cash flow negative even with no debt

worked.title: Koka Flour Mills: sustainable debt (Birr millions a year)

rows.label: Normalised sales, wheat price passed through
Operating cash flow before debt service

worked.note: Koka is viable but over-indebted: it can service about half of its current schedule. The structure must change, or part of the debt must be repaid from assets.

scenario.title: A cooperative owner, a negative business
scenario.situation: Habtamu Girma, owner of a cold store in Bishoftu, is cooperative and offers his house as extra collateral. The cold store's operating cash flow has been negative for 18 months because its main export buyer left, and no replacement contract is in sight.
scenario.question: What workout path fits best?
options: Treat the business as not viable and agree a voluntary sale or other exit, using the extra collateral to reduce loss
Restructure over 10 years because the owner is cooperative
Inject a new working capital loan
Do nothing until a new buyer appears
scenario.explain: Cooperation matters, but without positive cash flow a longer schedule only delays loss. An orderly exit with the extra collateral preserves the most value.

lessons.title: Restructuring options
body: Once the business is judged viable, the package is built from the options a typical bank manual lists: extending the repayment period, converting an overdraft into a term loan, adding or changing collateral, cross-collateralising loans, new covenants, transferring the loan to a stronger buyer, voluntary sale of assets, management changes, a co-manager placed by the bank, reducing limits and new personal guarantees from owners.

An injection of new money is the most dangerous option and the manual allows it only in exceptional cases: the analysis must show it is essential, collateral must be sufficient, the working capital gap must be backed by work orders or sales contracts, and repayment capacity must be clear.

items.label: Extend tenor
items.text: Match installments to sustainable cash flow

items.label: Convert
items.text: Hard-core overdraft into an amortising term loan

items.label: Sell assets
items.text: Voluntary sale of non-core assets to cut debt

items.label: More security
items.text: Additional collateral and owner guarantees

items.label: Management
items.text: Co-manager or management change

items.label: New money
items.text: Only in exceptional, well-evidenced cases

scenario.title: Designing Koka's package
scenario.situation: Koka can afford about Birr 36.8 million of debt service a year. It owns an unpledged warehouse in Adama worth about Birr 60 million and still has a strong buyer base.
scenario.question: Which package best preserves value?
options: Extend the full Birr 240 million over 15 years with no other change
Inject Birr 50 million of new working capital
Sell or swap the warehouse to cut debt by about Birr 60 million, convert the overdraft into a term loan and reschedule the rest to fit Birr 36.8 million a year, with tighter covenants
scenario.explain: Using the unpledged asset reduces debt to a level the cash flow can carry, and covenants protect the rest. A very long extension leaves the bank overexposed; new money and foreclosure both destroy value here.

example.title: Writing the commitment down
example.text: During negotiation Koka's general manager, Ayantu Bekele, promised monthly sales reports and that 80% of sales would be routed through Bank A. The workout analyst put both into the restructuring agreement as covenants, together with Koka's written admission of default and its undertaking to repay the restructured balance. When reports arrived late in month four, the bank had a written basis to act.

lessons.title: How NBE treats restructured loans
body: Restructuring changes the schedule, not the history. Under SBB/90/2024 a restructured NPL stays non-performing and on non-accrual until it earns its way back through a period of actual repayment. Banks report restructured loans to NBE, and a quarterly report covers each restructured loan of 5% of capital or more.

The rules stop banks from using repeated restructuring to hide problems: a non-performing exposure restructured more than twice is automatically classified at least substandard. A workout analyst who promises the business line that restructuring will clean the loan overnight is setting the bank up for a supervisory finding.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024, as reproduced in a typical bank manual
regulation.text: A non-accrual loan may return to performing and accrual status only when all of these hold at once: the counterparty has no exposure more than 90 days past due; installments have been paid on time for at least 6 consecutive months (monthly loans), 2 consecutive quarters (quarterly), 2 periods (semi-annual) or 1 period (annual); full repayment is now likely; the exposure is not defaulted or impaired; and all accrued interest has been paid. NPLs restructured more than twice are at least substandard. Restructured loans of 5% of capital or more are reported quarterly.

worked.title: Can Koka's restructured loan be upgraded in month 7? (monthly installments)

rows.label: Consecutive on-time monthly payments since restructuring
Any exposure above 90 days past due
Full repayment likely on new terms
Result
rows.value: Stays non-performing until the Birr 4 million is paid

worked.note: All tests must be met at the same time; one failure keeps the loan on non-accrual.

scenario.title: The third restructuring
scenario.situation: Mekele Metal Works PLC was restructured in 2024 and again in 2025. It now asks for a third restructuring and promises to repay on time. The business line asks to classify it special mention after signing.
scenario.question: How must the loan be classified after a third restructuring?
options: Pass, because it is current on the new schedule
At least substandard, and doubtful or loss if the days-past-due criteria call for it
Special mention, as the business line asks
It cannot be restructured, so it must be written off
scenario.explain: An NPL restructured more than twice is automatically at least substandard under SBB/90/2024. A third restructuring is allowed but cannot improve the classification.

lessons.title: Debt-to-asset swaps and foreclosed assets
body: In a debt-to-asset swap the borrower transfers a property to the bank, or sells it under the bank's control, in full or partial settlement of the debt. It can be faster and cheaper than foreclosure, but it converts a loan into an asset the bank must hold, insure, guard and sell. The question is always net value: what the asset will fetch, less costs and the time it takes.

Foreclosed and acquired assets need their own management: independent valuation, insurance in the bank's name, a sale plan with target dates, and reporting of the holding to management. A typical bank manual sells foreclosed collateral at public auction for cash, the winner paying within 15 days, and may partially finance buyers where the bank is the only mortgagee, for vehicles up to 50% of the floor price.

worked.title: Koka: rescue versus foreclosure, present value at 16% (Birr millions)

rows.label: Foreclosure: forced-sale value of mill and building
less legal, auction and holding costs
Rescue: warehouse swap now, net of costs
plus 36.8 a year for 5 years, discounted
less a 15% allowance for re-default risk on the stream

worked.note: Even after allowing for re-default, the rescue is worth about Birr 46 million more than foreclosure. That is the number to put before the committee.

example.title: The Adama warehouse swap
example.text: Koka transferred its unpledged Adama warehouse to Bank A, valued by the bank's engineer at Birr 60 million. The bank credited Birr 56 million, the value net of transfer and selling costs, to the loan. Meron's team insured the warehouse, leased it short term to a grain trader to cover costs, and set a sale target of nine months, reporting the holding monthly until it was sold.

scenario.title: Accepting an asset at book value
scenario.situation: A borrower offers to settle Birr 30 million of debt with a half-finished hotel in Bahir Dar. Its owner values it at Birr 30 million; the bank's engineer estimates a forced sale at Birr 18 million after 2 years.
scenario.question: How should the bank evaluate the offer?
options: Accept at Birr 30 million, the owner's value
Value it at the engineer's net realisable value, discounted for time and costs, and compare with other recovery routes
scenario.explain: A swap is worth the net, time-adjusted value the bank can realise, not the owner's figure. The shortfall is a loss to recognise now, not later.

lessons.title: Foreclosure, court and write-off
body: When negotiation fails, Ethiopian law gives banks a strong tool: the law on property mortgaged or pledged with banks (reported as Proclamation No. 97/1998, amended by No. 216/2000) lets a bank foreclose and auction mortgaged or pledged property without first going to court. Clean loans, guarantees and shortfalls after auction go through litigation instead. Security over movables is registered under the Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019.

A typical manual recommends foreclosure when the borrower will not negotiate, cash flow has collapsed, rescheduled terms are broken, documents are withheld, the limitation period will expire in under a year, or the collateral is being damaged. A borrower may suspend foreclosure for up to three months with a minimum down payment, for example accrued interest plus 10% of principal after a 30-day legal notice has expired. Write-off comes only after all recovery routes are exhausted, with full provision held, and the claim is still pursued afterwards.

items.label: Legal notice
items.text: 30-day notice to pay before foreclosure

items.label: Suspension window
items.text: Up to 3 months against a minimum down payment

items.label: Auction
items.text: Public auction for cash; winner pays within 15 days

items.label: Shortfall
items.text: Litigation for other attachable property

items.label: Write-off
items.text: Board-approved above the management limit; post write-off follow-up continues

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (August 2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual allows write-off only after recovery is exhausted and proved impossible or uneconomic: insolvency or bankruptcy, a shortfall after auction with no attachable property, a final court judgment against the bank, or an elapsed limitation period. Evidence of no property comes from municipal, trade and transport offices. Management approves write-offs up to Birr 15 million of principal, the board above it; a partial write-off leaves Birr 1,000 on the books, and recovery efforts continue after write-off.

example.title: After the auction
example.text: Bank A auctioned the trucks of Tesfaye Freight PLC, which owed Birr 46 million. The auction raised Birr 31 million. The workout unit sued on the owner's personal guarantee and searched transport and land records for other assets, finding a plot worth Birr 6 million. Only after that judgment was enforced did it table the remaining Birr 9 million for write-off, fully provided, with a note to keep pursuing the claim.

takeaways: Workout starts at the watch list, with a documented reminder sequence and written commitments
Viability comes first: rescue viable businesses, exit non-viable ones early
Compare rescue and foreclosure on a present-value basis, after costs and re-default risk
Restructured NPLs stay on non-accrual until every SBB/90/2024 upgrade test is met; more than two restructurings means at least substandard
Debt-to-asset swaps and foreclosed assets are valued at net realisable value and sold to a plan
Write-off follows exhausted recovery and full provision; the claim is still pursued

quiz.q: Under SBB/90/2024, when must a customer's other exposures be reclassified because of one NPL?
options: When the NPL is 20% or more of the customer's exposure
When the NPL is 5% or more of the customer's exposure
Only when all loans are past due
quiz.explain: The cross-default rule applies at 20% or more of the customer's exposure.

quiz.q: A monthly-installment restructured NPL can be upgraded after how many consecutive on-time payments, if all other tests are met?
quiz.explain: Monthly loans need at least 6 consecutive on-time payments.

quiz.q: An NPL restructured for the third time is classified:
quiz.explain: More than two restructurings means at least substandard.

quiz.q: Cash available for debt service is Birr 46 million and the target DSCR is 1.25. What annual debt service is affordable?
Under a typical manual, a new money injection into an NPL needs:
options: Evidence it is essential, sufficient collateral, contracts backing the working capital gap and clear repayment capacity
Nothing if the loan is restructured
quiz.explain: The manual allows injection only in exceptional, evidenced cases.

quiz.q: Foreclosed property will sell for Birr 140 million net in 18 months. At 16%, its present value is about:

modules.title: IFRS 9 in the portfolio
modules.summary: Stage the book, recognise significant increases in credit risk, compute expected credit loss with forward-looking scenarios, and reconcile IFRS 9 with SBB/90/2024 minimum provisions.
objectives: Assign loans to IFRS 9 Stage 1, 2 or 3 and explain the effect on the loss allowance
Identify significant increase in credit risk from quantitative and qualitative triggers
Compute expected credit loss as PD x LGD x EAD and weight it across forward-looking scenarios
Reconcile IFRS 9 allowances with SBB/90/2024 minimum provisions and the regulatory reserve

lessons.title: Three stages of credit quality
body: IFRS 9, adopted in Ethiopia through the financial reporting framework that requires IFRS, makes banks provide for losses they expect, not only those already incurred. Every loan sits in one of three stages. Stage 1 loans carry a 12-month expected loss. Stage 2 loans, where credit risk has increased significantly since the loan was made, carry a lifetime expected loss. Stage 3 loans are credit-impaired and also carry a lifetime loss, with interest recognised on the net amount.

The jump from 12 months to lifetime is the cliff that makes staging matter. Moving a five-year loan from Stage 1 to Stage 2 can multiply its allowance several times, even though the borrower has not defaulted.

items.label: Stage 1: performing
items.text: No significant increase in credit risk; 12-month ECL

items.label: Stage 2: underperforming
items.text: Significant increase in credit risk; lifetime ECL

items.label: Stage 3: credit-impaired
items.text: Default or impairment; lifetime ECL, interest on net carrying amount

example.title: Mapping NBE categories to stages
example.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual defines pass as exposures with no significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition, and special mention as exposures where credit risk has increased significantly. Bank A therefore starts by mapping pass to Stage 1, special mention to Stage 2 and the three NPL categories to Stage 3, then overrides the mapping where its own early warning signals show a significant increase in risk on a loan that is still pass.

scenario.title: A pass loan with a warning
scenario.situation: Tana Steel Works PLC is current on all payments, so it is pass under SBB/90/2024. But its imported input costs have risen sharply after birr depreciation and its projected DSCR has fallen from 1.40 to 0.80.
scenario.question: Which IFRS 9 stage is right?
options: No stage until it misses a payment
Stage 2, because credit risk has increased significantly even without arrears
scenario.explain: Staging looks at the change in default risk, not only at arrears. A collapse in projected coverage is a significant increase in credit risk, so lifetime ECL applies.

lessons.title: Significant increase in credit risk
body: IFRS 9 does not define significant increase in credit risk with one number, so each bank writes its own policy. It combines a quantitative test, such as an internal grade downgrade of two or more notches or a lifetime PD that has doubled since origination, with qualitative triggers and a backstop: under IFRS 9 there is a rebuttable presumption that a loan more than 30 days past due has had a significant increase.

Qualitative triggers come straight from the watch list: covenant breaches, a hard-core overdraft, a sector under stress, a restructuring request, adverse Credit Reference Bureau information or a large borrower's group in trouble. A watch list that is not linked to staging leaves the allowance too low.

items.label: Rating downgrade
items.text: Two or more notches since origination

items.label: 30 days past due
items.text: The IFRS 9 backstop presumption

items.label: Watch list
items.text: Every watch-listed loan reviewed for Stage 2

items.label: Covenant breach
items.text: DSCR or leverage covenant broken

items.label: Restructuring request
items.text: Borrower asks to change terms

items.label: Group contagion
items.text: Another group company is in default

scenario.title: A covenant breach in a troubled group
scenario.situation: Hawassa Textiles PLC is current but has breached its leverage covenant. Hawassa Yarn PLC, a sister company under the same controlling owner, is 95 days past due.
scenario.question: How should Hawassa Textiles be staged?
options: Stage 2 at least, because of the covenant breach and the default in the group
Remove it from the ECL model
scenario.explain: A covenant breach and a defaulted sister company are clear qualitative signs of increased risk. Whether it moves to Stage 3 depends on the bank's default definition and the cross-default analysis.

lessons.tip: Report how many loans entered Stage 2 on qualitative triggers alone; if the number is near zero, the watch list is not feeding the model.

lessons.title: Expected credit loss: PD x LGD x EAD
body: Expected credit loss multiplies three estimates. Probability of default (PD) is the chance the borrower defaults over the horizon: 12 months for Stage 1, the remaining life for Stage 2. Loss given default (LGD) is the share of the exposure lost after recoveries from collateral, net of costs and time. Exposure at default (EAD) is what will be owed when default happens, including expected drawdowns of undrawn limits.

Ethiopian banks have short and patchy default histories, so PDs are often built from internal ratings and the bank's own migration data, and LGDs from past recoveries on foreclosed collateral. The data quality work in module 1 is what makes these numbers credible.

visual.caption: Horizon: 12 months in Stage 1, lifetime in Stages 2 and 3 (PD of 100% in Stage 3).

worked.title: Tana Steel Works PLC: the cliff from Stage 1 to Stage 2 (Birr millions)

rows.label: Exposure at default (drawn plus expected drawdown)
Increase in allowance from staging alone

worked.note: Moving one large borrower to Stage 2 adds Birr 84 million to the allowance, about 0.9% of Bank A's capital, without a single missed payment.

example.title: Building LGD from recoveries
example.text: Bank A's risk team reviewed 140 foreclosures over five years. Buildings in Addis Ababa recovered about 70% of the exposure after costs, with a median of 20 months from legal notice to cash; trucks recovered about 45% within 8 months. Discounting the cash flows gave LGDs of about 40% for building-secured loans and 60% for truck loans, replacing a single 45% assumption.

lessons.title: Forward-looking scenarios
body: IFRS 9 requires ECL to reflect reasonable forecasts of future conditions, not only the past. Banks build a base, a downside and an upside scenario for the variables that drive defaults in Ethiopia, such as the exchange rate, inflation, the National Bank Rate, rainfall and key export prices, and compute ECL under each.

The reported ECL is the probability-weighted average. Because losses rise faster in bad times than they fall in good ones, the weighted figure is usually above the base case. Scenario weights and assumptions should be approved by management and disclosed.

worked.title: Bank A probability-weighted ECL, June 2026 (Birr billions)

rows.label: Base: inflation easing, birr stable in real terms, ECL 2.40, weight 60%
Downside: 30% depreciation and inflation spike, ECL 3.00, weight 30%
Upside: strong coffee prices, ECL 1.80, weight 10%

worked.note: The weighted ECL of Birr 2.52 billion is the IFRS 9 loss allowance shown in the module 1 dashboard.

scenario.title: Choosing scenario weights
scenario.situation: In September 2026 the business director proposes weights of 80% upside, 20% base and 0% downside, which would cut ECL by Birr 0.4 billion and lift profit. Inflation had risen to 13.4% in May 2026 and the policy rate had just been raised.
scenario.question: What should the risk team say?
options: Reject: weights must reflect a balanced, evidence-based view of conditions, and current data does not support dropping the downside
Accept: the director knows the market
scenario.explain: Scenario weights are a judgment that must be supportable and unbiased. Removing the downside when inflation and rates are rising would understate expected losses.

lessons.title: Reconciling IFRS 9 and SBB/90/2024
body: Ethiopian banks run two numbers side by side. The IFRS 9 allowance goes into the financial statements. The SBB/90/2024 minimum provision is a regulatory floor computed loan by loan from the classification, with the deductions the directive allows. When the IFRS 9 figure is the lower of the two, the bank does not raise its accounting allowance; it holds the difference in a non-distributable regulatory reserve within equity.

That reserve cannot be paid out as dividends. It protects depositors from an optimistic model, and it gives management a clear incentive to keep IFRS 9 estimates realistic. When the IFRS 9 figure is higher, it simply stands, and no reserve is needed.

regulation.text: Where the provision computed under IFRS is below the minimum required by the directive, the difference is transferred to a non-distributable regulatory reserve. In computing the minimum, a typical bank manual notes that banks may deduct interest held in suspense and the lower of net recoverable value or estimated collateral value of physical collateral, but each NPL must still carry at least 3% of its outstanding balance.

worked.title: Bank A reconciliation, June 2026 (Birr billions)

rows.label: SBB/90/2024 minimum, loan by loan after allowed deductions
Shortfall of IFRS 9 below the minimum

worked.note: The regulatory reserve does not change reported loan values, but it locks up equity. A model that understates losses therefore costs shareholders dividends anyway.

scenario.title: Loss loan with strong collateral
scenario.situation: A loss-category loan of Birr 10 million is backed by a building whose lower of net recoverable and estimated value is Birr 12 million.
scenario.question: What is the SBB/90/2024 minimum provision on this loan?
options: Zero, because collateral exceeds the loan
Birr 0.3 million, the 3% floor for an NPL
scenario.explain: After deducting collateral nothing is left to provide at 100%, but each NPL must carry at least 3% of its outstanding balance: 3% x 10 = 0.3 million.

lessons.title: Explaining the numbers to management
body: Executives see two provision figures, two sets of categories and a reserve, and they ask which one is real. The portfolio manager's job is to show both on one page with a bridge from the last quarter: new loans, stage transfers, write-offs, changes in scenarios and model updates, and the regulatory reserve at the bottom.
Keep the language simple. IFRS 9 is the bank's best estimate of expected loss; SBB/90/2024 is the regulator's minimum; the reserve is the gap, held in equity.

left.title: IFRS 9
items: PD x LGD x EAD with scenarios

right.title: SBB/90/2024
items: Pass to loss by days past due and criteria
Fixed minimum rates after allowed deductions
Shortfall held in a regulatory reserve

example.title: The quarter's allowance bridge
example.text: Meron presented the Q3 bridge: opening allowance Birr 2.52 billion, plus 0.15 from new loans, plus 0.31 from transfers into Stage 2 led by import-dependent manufacturers, plus 0.22 from new Stage 3 loans, minus 0.12 of write-offs, minus 0.08 from recoveries, closing at Birr 3.00 billion. The regulatory minimum had risen to 2.95 billion, so the reserve was no longer needed. Executives could see in one line why provisions rose.

scenario.title: Releasing the reserve
scenario.situation: After a quarter of heavy Stage 2 transfers, Bank A's IFRS 9 allowance is Birr 3.00 billion and the SBB/90/2024 minimum is Birr 2.95 billion. The regulatory reserve from the previous quarter stands at Birr 0.18 billion.
scenario.question: What happens to the regulatory reserve?
options: It is no longer required because IFRS 9 is now above the minimum, and can be released according to policy
It is charged to profit and loss
scenario.explain: The reserve covers only a shortfall of IFRS 9 below the minimum. Once IFRS 9 exceeds the minimum, no reserve is required.

takeaways: Stage 1 carries 12-month ECL; Stages 2 and 3 carry lifetime ECL, which creates a cliff
Significant increase in credit risk combines rating changes, the 30-day backstop and watch-list triggers
ECL = PD x LGD x EAD, weighted across base, downside and upside scenarios
When IFRS 9 is below the SBB/90/2024 minimum, the gap goes to a non-distributable regulatory reserve (Art. 11)
Every NPL carries at least 3% even when collateral covers it
Present one bridge that explains both numbers to management

quiz.q: Which IFRS 9 stage carries a 12-month expected credit loss?
quiz.explain: Only Stage 1 uses a 12-month horizon.

quiz.q: EAD Birr 200 million, lifetime PD 15%, LGD 50%. What is the lifetime ECL?
quiz.explain: 15% x 50% x 200 = 15 million.

quiz.q: Under IFRS 9 the rebuttable presumption of a significant increase in credit risk applies when a loan is more than:
quiz.explain: The 30-day backstop is an IFRS 9 presumption.

quiz.q: IFRS 9 allowance Birr 1.8 billion; SBB/90/2024 minimum Birr 2.1 billion. What happens?
options: Allowance raised to 2.1 billion through profit and loss
Birr 0.3 billion is held in a non-distributable regulatory reserve
quiz.explain: SBB/90/2024 Art. 11 sends the shortfall to a regulatory reserve.

quiz.q: Scenario ECLs: base 2.0 (weight 50%), downside 3.0 (40%), upside 1.5 (10%). Weighted ECL?
A typical bank manual maps which NBE category to significant increase in credit risk?
quiz.explain: The manual defines special mention as exposures with a significant increase in credit risk.

modules.title: Stress testing, reporting and the portfolio review
modules.summary: Stress the book under Ethiopian scenarios, translate losses into capital, build dashboards and reports for management, ALCO, the board and NBE, and present the capstone portfolio review.
objectives: Design Ethiopian stress scenarios and run a birr depreciation stress test on a loan book
Translate stressed losses into NPL, provision and capital ratio effects
Build a portfolio dashboard and the reports owed to ALCO, the board and NBE
Present a remediation plan in a portfolio review

lessons.title: Designing stress scenarios for Ethiopia
body: A stress test asks what happens to the book if a severe but plausible event occurs. For Ethiopian banks the relevant shocks are well known: a sharp birr depreciation under the market-based exchange rate regime, an inflation spike, a drought, a disruption that halts trade in one region, and a fall in the price of a key export such as coffee. Each hits specific sectors and borrowers, not the whole book evenly.

Good scenarios name the transmission channel: depreciation raises the Birr cost of imported inputs and foreign-currency debt; inflation squeezes consumers and raises funding costs; drought cuts agricultural income and food processors' supply; a regional disruption stops sales and access to collateral.

items.label: Birr depreciation
items.text: Importers, import-dependent manufacturers, construction

items.label: Inflation spike
items.text: Retail borrowers, margins, funding costs

items.label: Drought
items.text: Agriculture, agro-processing, rural trade

items.label: Regional disruption
items.text: Trade and transport in the affected region; collateral access

items.label: Commodity price fall
items.text: Coffee and oilseed exporters and their suppliers

regulation.text: The guidelines expect banks to manage credit, liquidity, market and operational risk through a risk management function and an Asset Liability Committee (ALCO), and to use stress testing to understand how adverse conditions would affect them. Trainers should check for any newer version of the guidelines.

example.title: Picking Bank A's scenarios
example.text: Meron's team chose three scenarios for the capstone: a 30% birr depreciation, a drought cutting agricultural output, and a fall in coffee export prices. They dropped a general recession scenario because it did not point to specific borrowers. Each scenario came with a one-page story of how it would reach Bank A's top 20 borrowers.

lessons.title: Running the depreciation stress test
body: Start at borrower level for the large names and at segment level for the rest. For each large import-dependent borrower, recompute cash flow with higher Birr input costs, allowing only the share of the increase it can pass on to customers. For the rest, apply a stressed default rate to the exposed segments.
Then convert new defaults into losses with LGD, and add the effect of stage transfers on the IFRS 9 allowance. Keep the method simple enough to explain to the board in two minutes.

worked.title: Tana Steel Works PLC under a 30% depreciation (Birr millions a year)

rows.label: Base cash available for debt service

worked.note: Tana Steel cannot service its debt under the scenario. It goes to the watch list now, with a covenant review and a talk about foreign currency planning.

scenario.title: Pass-through assumption
scenario.situation: The relationship manager says Tana Steel can pass on 100% of any cost increase because steel prices in Addis Ababa follow import costs. Last year, after a smaller depreciation, it passed on about 40% within the first year.
scenario.question: Which pass-through should the stress test use?
options: About 40%, supported by the borrower's own recent history, with 100% shown only as a sensitivity
scenario.explain: Stress assumptions should rest on evidence. The borrower's own recent pass-through is the best guide; the optimistic case can be shown as a sensitivity.

lessons.title: From stressed losses to capital
body: The board does not ask how many loans fail; it asks whether the bank stays above its capital minimum. Add stressed new NPLs to the current stock, compute extra provisions, deduct them from capital and recompute the capital ratio. If the ratio falls below the 11% minimum under SBB/95/2025, or below the internal buffer, the plan must show how capital would be restored.
Remember second-round effects: defaulted exposures can carry a 150% risk weight, which raises risk-weighted assets just as capital falls.

worked.title: Bank A: 30% depreciation scenario (Birr billions)

rows.label: FX-exposed loans: import 9.0 + half of manufacturing 6.0
Stressed default rate on exposed loans
Capital after losses, before tax effects: 9.60 - 1.01

worked.note: Bank A would breach the minimum by about 0.3 points even before higher risk weights on defaulted loans. The remediation plan must build a buffer now.

scenario.title: Responding to the stress result
scenario.situation: The stress test shows Bank A's total capital ratio falling to 10.7% under a 30% depreciation. The CFO suggests leaving it out of the board pack because the scenario may never happen.
scenario.question: What should the portfolio manager do?
options: Change the scenario to 10% so the ratio stays above 11%
Present it with a remediation plan: reduce FX-exposed concentration, retain earnings, review pricing and prepare capital options
scenario.explain: The point of a stress test is to act before the event. Hiding or softening the result defeats its purpose; the board needs the result and the plan.

lessons.title: Dashboards that managers read
body: A portfolio dashboard fits on one page and answers four questions: how big is the book and how is it growing, how good is it, where is it concentrated, and are we inside our limits? Each indicator shows the current value, the trend over the last four quarters and a traffic light against the risk appetite.

Branch and unit dashboards use the same design with local figures: past-due buckets, watch-list loans, collections against target, expiring overdrafts and insurance, and NPLs by officer. The work assignment in this course asks you to build exactly this for your own branch or unit.

items.label: Size
items.text: Gross loans, growth, approvals pipeline

items.label: Quality
items.text: NPL ratio, special mention, roll rates, coverage

items.label: Concentration
items.text: Top 20, large exposures, sector HHI

items.label: Limits
items.text: Traffic lights against appetite and NBE limits

example.title: The Adama branch dashboard
example.text: Branch manager Tigist Worku built a one-page dashboard for her Adama branch: Birr 1.9 billion of loans, 4.1% NPL, Birr 120 million in the 30 to 89 day buckets, 14 watch-list loans with owners and next actions, 9 insurance policies expiring within a month, and collections at 93% of target. At the weekly meeting the team spent its time on the 14 names, not on reading tables.

lessons.tip: If a dashboard needs a page of footnotes, it has too many indicators; keep ten or fewer.

lessons.title: Reporting to ALCO, the board and NBE
body: Different audiences need different cuts of the same data. Management and ALCO need monthly detail on quality, concentration, pricing and the funding behind loan growth. The board needs a quarterly view against the risk appetite, large and related-party exposures, the stress test and the remediation progress. NBE receives prescribed returns on fixed deadlines.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual lists the returns its portfolio unit produces for NBE: disbursements and collections, related-party returns, borrowers above 10% of capital, loans by status, classification and provisioning, NPLs by sector and branch, the top 20 NPLs and twenty largest borrowers, restructured loans and loans re-categorized from non-accrual to accrual of 5% of capital or more, and off-balance sheet provisions.

regulation.source: NBE Directives No. SBB/87/2024 and SBB/90/2024
regulation.text: Large exposures are reported to NBE monthly within 20 days, and breaches immediately. Restructured loans of 5% of the bank's capital or more are reported quarterly. Off-balance sheet exposures carry general provisions, for example 2% on guarantees without counter guarantee, letters of credit and loan commitments, as reproduced in a typical bank manual.

items.text: Branch and unit dashboards; watch-list actions

items.label: Monthly
items.text: Management and ALCO pack; NBE large-exposure return within 20 days

items.label: Quarterly
items.text: Board risk report; classification and provisioning; restructured loans of 5% of capital or more

items.label: Annually
items.text: Risk appetite review, limit recalibration, stress test refresh

scenario.title: A breach discovered mid-month
scenario.situation: On 9 October Meron discovers that the Gedeo group is at 27.1% of capital, above the 25% limit. The next monthly large-exposure return is due on 20 October.
scenario.question: When should NBE be informed?
options: In the next monthly return on 20 October
Immediately, as a breach, with the remediation plan to follow
scenario.explain: SBB/87/2024 requires breaches to be reported immediately, separate from the routine monthly return.

lessons.title: Capstone: Bank A's portfolio review
body: In the capstone you receive Bank A's 2,000-loan dataset as a spreadsheet. Working in a group, you reconcile it to the ledger, rebuild connected groups, compute the indicators, vintage and migration tables and concentration measures, test limits, stage the book, run the depreciation stress test and present a remediation plan to a panel acting as the board risk committee.

The course is assessed on the portfolio review presentation (40%), a test (30%), a work assignment in which you build a dashboard for your own branch or unit (20%) and participation (10%). The pass mark is 70%.

items.label: Clean
items.text: Reconcile 2,000 loans to the ledger; fix codes; merge duplicates

items.label: Analyse
items.text: Indicators, vintages, migration, roll rates, HHI, top 20

items.label: Test
items.text: Large exposures, related parties, sector limits

items.label: Stress
items.text: 30% depreciation: NPLs, provisions, capital ratio

items.label: Plan
items.text: Remediation actions, owners, dates and targets

worked.title: Remediation plan summary for Bank A

rows.label: Gedeo group at 27.1% of capital
rows.value: Sell a Birr 0.7 billion participation; target 19.8% in 6 months

rows.label: Special mention Birr 4.52 billion
rows.value: Collection team on 60 to 89 days; target cure rate 40%

rows.label: Stressed capital ratio 10.7%
rows.value: Retain FY2026 profits; FX-exposed new lending capped

rows.label: Regulatory reserve Birr 0.18 billion
rows.value: Review model and scenario weights; no release until IFRS 9 above minimum

rows.label: Data error rate 1% of balances
rows.value: Monthly ledger reconciliation and sector code audit

worked.note: Every finding has an action, an owner, a date and a measurable target. That is what the panel grades.

example.title: A winning presentation
example.text: One group opened with a single slide: three problems, three numbers, three actions. They showed the Gedeo breach, the 9.6% stressed NPL ratio and the 10.7% stressed capital ratio, then spent the rest of their 15 minutes on the remediation plan and its dates. When the panel challenged their 15% stressed default rate, they showed the 2024 depreciation history of import borrowers in the dataset that supported it.

scenario.title: The panel's toughest question
scenario.situation: During your presentation the panel asks why you recommend selling a participation in the Gedeo group rather than simply asking the group to repay Birr 0.2 billion.
scenario.question: Which answer is strongest?
options: Repaying 0.2 billion would only reach the 25% legal limit with no buffer; the participation brings the group under the 20% internal limit without forcing a healthy borrower to cut working capital
Because the group is in default
scenario.explain: The answer links the action to both the legal and internal limits and to the borrower's health. That is the reasoning a board expects.

takeaways: Ethiopian stress scenarios should name the channel: depreciation, inflation, drought, regional disruption, commodity prices
Stress results matter in capital terms: compare the stressed ratio with the 11% minimum and the internal buffer
A one-page dashboard covers size, quality, concentration and limits with trends and traffic lights
Large-exposure breaches go to NBE immediately; routine returns follow fixed deadlines
A remediation plan gives every finding an action, owner, date and target

quiz.q: Base cash available Birr 420 million, debt service Birr 300 million. Input costs rise Birr 300 million and 40% is passed through. Stressed DSCR?
Which sectors are hit first by a sharp birr depreciation?
quiz.explain: Higher Birr cost of imports hits importers and manufacturers using imported inputs.

quiz.q: Capital Birr 9.6 billion, extra provisions Birr 1.01 billion, RWA Birr 80 billion. Stressed total capital ratio?
Under SBB/87/2024, a large-exposure breach is reported:
quiz.explain: Breaches are reported immediately.

quiz.q: In this course's assessment, the portfolio review presentation is worth:
quiz.explain: Presentation 40%, test 30%, dashboard assignment 20%, participation 10%.

quiz.q: Under the NBE Risk Management Guidelines, which committee oversees balance sheet and funding risk alongside credit growth?
quiz.explain: The Asset Liability Committee manages balance sheet and liquidity risk.

exam.q: Bank A's special mention balance is Birr 4.52 billion; 20% migrated to NPL last quarter. If the same rate holds, how much new NPL comes from special mention next quarter?
A book is 40% trade, 40% manufacturing and 20% construction. Its sector HHI is:
exam.explain: 1,600 + 1,600 + 400 = 3,600, high concentration.

exam.q: Vintage FY2024 shows 3.9% of balances 90+ days past due at 12 months; FY2023 showed 2.4% at 12 months. The most likely conclusion is:
options: Underwriting or market conditions for the FY2024 loans were weaker
The difference is caused by book growth
Nothing can be concluded from vintages
exam.explain: Same-age comparison isolates origination quality.

exam.q: Four companies with common controlling shareholders and cross guarantees owe Birr 0.9, 0.7, 0.6 and 0.4 billion. Total capital is Birr 9.6 billion. Under SBB/87/2024 the group is:
options: Within the limit, since each company is below 10%
At 27.1% of capital, above the 25% limit

exam.q: Aggregate related-party exposure is Birr 3.10 billion and total capital Birr 9.6 billion. What is the largest new related-party loan possible within the SBB/88/2024 aggregate limit?
Which loan of Birr 100 million consumes the most capital under SBB/95/2025?
options: Unrated SME with sales under Birr 90 million
exam.explain: 150% x 11% = 16.5 million, the highest.

exam.q: Capital is expected to be Birr 10.8 billion and the internal target ratio 12.5%. Current RWA is Birr 80 billion. RWA headroom is:
After the credit growth cap was removed in July 2026, which factor most directly limits Bank A's loan growth?
options: Capital headroom, funding and the bank's own risk appetite, with a possible targeted reserve requirement linked to the loan-to-deposit ratio
exam.explain: Capital, funding and appetite now set the budget; there is no minimum deposit rate since NBE/INT/13/2026.

exam.q: A borrower has a term loan of Birr 50 million that is 120 days past due and an overdraft of Birr 150 million that is performing. Does the cross-default rule apply?
options: Yes: the NPL is 25% of total exposure
exam.explain: 50 / 200 = 25%, which is 20% or more.

exam.q: A quarterly-installment restructured NPL has paid two consecutive quarters on time, has no exposure over 90 days past due and is likely to repay in full, but Birr 2 million of old accrued interest is unpaid. Can it be upgraded?
options: No: all accrued interest must be paid before upgrade
exam.explain: Every SBB/90/2024 upgrade test must be met at the same time.

exam.q: Rescue is valued at Birr 158 million and foreclosure at Birr 112 million, both in present value. The workout committee should normally:
options: Choose the rescue, with covenants and monitoring, since it preserves about Birr 46 million more
Wait for the borrower to propose
exam.explain: Workout principles favour the option with the higher net present value for viable businesses.

exam.q: A borrower offers a property worth Birr 30 million by its own estimate in settlement; the bank's engineer estimates a net forced-sale value of Birr 18 million in 2 years. At what basis should the swap be valued?
options: Birr 18 million discounted for 2 years and costs
exam.explain: Swaps are valued at net, time-adjusted realisable value.

exam.q: Under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, which is NOT a ground for write-off?
options: Final appellate judgment against the bank
The borrower is 100 days past due
Shortfall after auction with no attachable property
exam.explain: Write-off follows exhausted recovery, not a simple delay.

exam.q: A Stage 1 loan with EAD Birr 500 million, 12-month PD 3% and LGD 40% moves to Stage 2 with lifetime PD 15%. By how much does its ECL rise?
exam.explain: Stage 1: 6 million; Stage 2: 30 million; increase 24 million.

exam.q: Which is the strongest qualitative trigger for moving a current loan to Stage 2?
options: A breached leverage covenant and a defaulted sister company in the same group
The loan is larger than average
The loan was approved at head office
exam.explain: Covenant breach and group default signal a significant increase in credit risk.

exam.q: IFRS 9 allowance Birr 2.52 billion; SBB/90/2024 minimum Birr 2.70 billion. What does Bank A record?
options: Raise the allowance to 2.70 through profit and loss
Keep the allowance at 2.52 and hold Birr 0.18 billion in a non-distributable regulatory reserve
exam.explain: SBB/90/2024 Art. 11 sends the shortfall to a regulatory reserve.

exam.q: A doubtful loan of Birr 40 million has collateral with a lower of net recoverable and estimated value of Birr 39 million. Its SBB/90/2024 minimum provision is:
exam.explain: (40 - 39) x 50% = 0.5 million, below the 3% floor of 1.2 million, so 1.2 million applies.

exam.q: FX-exposed loans of Birr 15 billion suffer a 15% stressed default rate with 45% LGD. Extra provisions are about:
Which dashboard design best serves a branch manager?
options: A one-page view of past-due buckets, watch-list names with actions, collections against target and expiring insurance, with trends
exam.explain: A short dashboard focused on action drives follow-up.

exam.q: A restructured loan to a single borrower equals 6% of Bank A's capital. What reporting applies?
options: It is included in NBE's quarterly report of restructured loans of 5% of capital or more
exam.explain: Restructured loans of 5% of capital or more are reported quarterly.
